newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi quoted as saying lira ERM return imminent.
newsitem.headline: Prodi quoted as saying lira ERM return imminent.

text.p: An Italian news agency on Friday quoted Prime Minister Romano Prodi as saying that the lira would return to Europe's exchange rate mechanism in a matter of "hours or days".

The AGI agency report followed growing indications that Italy had asked for a meeting on Saturday of the European Union's monetary committee to put the currency back into the currency grid it left in 1992.
AGI, and later the news agency ANSA, quoted Prodi as saying in Sicily, where he is on a visit, that the lira's return to the ERM was a matter of "a few hours or a few days".

"We said that once the budget was approved the framework would be in place to start technical negotiations," ANSA quoted Prodi as saying. "That is the way it is going. These are not formal negotiations. We are exchanging the necessary data for a lira return to the ERM."
Italy's 1997 austerity budget was approved by the lower house of parliament last Saturday and is now going through the Senate, where Prodi's centre-left government has a secure majority.
Earlier, a senior source told Reuters in Frankfurt that the Italian government had asked for a meeting of the EU monetary committee on Saturday to discuss the terms of a lira re-entry.
